High throttling with comfortable CPU usage points to CFS throttling, and the common cause is threads sized to the node instead of the container limit.","likely_cause":"Thread‑count (GOMAXPROCS/WEB_CONCURRENCY) set to node core count causing CFS throttling","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"High throttling periods with low average CPU indicate throttling, not real load","evidence_ids":["RB-002#0","RB-002#1"],"quote":"If a service's p99 latency climbs while its CPU graph looks comfortable, suspect CFS throttling before anything else."},{"text":"The usual trigger for such throttling is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2"],"quote":"The usual trigger is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container."},{"text":"Check GOMAXPROCS (for Go) or WEB_CONCURRENCY (for Python) inside the pod to confirm mismatch","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2","RB-002#2"],"quote":"Go before 1.25 sets GOMAXPROCS to the node's core count, not the container limit"}],"next_checks":["View Grafana \"Container CPU\" panel in throttling mode; alert if >25% periods","Run kubectl exec <pod> -- cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat and compare nr_throttled vs nr_periods","Exec into the pod and printenv GOMAXPROCS to see if it exceeds the container limit","Exec into the fraud‑scorer pod and check WEB_CONCURRENCY value","If mismatch found, lower thread count (GOMAXPROCS or WEB_CONCURRENCY) to match CPU limit and monitor throttling reduction"]}
